sentences.text: JUDGMENT 1.

The present claim proceedings have emanated from Detailed Accident Report (hereinafter referred to as DAR), as filed on 04.09.2019, with reference to FIR No. 121/2019, registered at PS Rani Bagh, Delhi, in respect of commission of offence of simple hurt, by rash and negligent driving of a motor vehicle, on a public road, punishable U/s 279/337 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as IPC).

Subsequently, a final report under Section 173 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (herein afterwards referred as Cr.P.C), was filed against respondent no. 1, namely Ishwar Singh (hereinafter referred as R1), for the alleged commission of offence under Section 279/337 of IPC.

Further, on 16.01.2020, a separate claim petition was filed by the petitioner, under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as M.V. Act), seeking compensation in the sum of Rs. 20,00,000/-, with interest at the rate of 18% per annum, in respect of simple injuries sustained by petitioner/ injured, as well as damage to his car, in a road traffic accident.
However, vide statement dated 11.12.2024, the petitioner stated that he wants to withdraw his claim, for the damage to his car, sustained in the case accident.
2. As per DAR, the offending vehicle was registered in the name of Director, FSL, Rohini, Delhi (hereinafter referred as R2) and Sh. Prakash Chandra, was impleaded as Authorized Representative of R2.

3. The brief facts of the case as discernible from the DAR, claim petition and documents of the petitioner, are that, on 21.03.2019, at about 9:30 p.m., when the petitioner was coming from Barsana, District Mathura, to Rohini Delhi, in his Honda City Car, bearing registration No.
DL-8CNA-4905 (herein after referred as victim's vehicle) and was taking turn at the red light signal of Madhuban Chowk, for going towards Sector 24, Rohini, his vehicle was hit by a Scorpio car,
bearing registration no. DL-8CAT-5595 (hereinafter referred as offending vehicle).
It was further averred that the offending vehicle was driven by its driver R1, at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without caring traffic rules.
It was further averred that as a result of the said impact, the air bags of the victim's vehicle got opened and the petitioner sustained injuries on his hands.

It was further averred that his car was badly damaged, after which, the petitioner/injured was taken to Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, Pitampura, Delhi, where he was medically examined, vide MLC no. 782/19, as per which, the injuries sustained by the petitioner were stated to be simple in nature.
4. The respondent no.1/driver of the offending vehicle and R2 failed to file written statement on record therefore, they deemed to have admitted the contents of the DAR/petition.

Further, the defence of R1 and R2 was struck off, vide order dated 19.05.2022.
5.

From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed by the Learned Predecessor Court, vide order dated 19.05.2022:-
1.

Whether on 21.03.2019 at about 9:30 pm, at Maduban Chowk, Delhi, one Scorpio Car bearing registration No. DL-8CAT-5595, which was being driven rashly and Navwal Singh vs Ishwar on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189250524/
4 negligently by R1/Ishwar Singh, jad hit the car bearing registration no.
DL-8CNA-4905 and caused the injuries to Nawal Singh?
OPP 2.
Whether petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
3. Relief.
6.
After framing of issues, opportunities were given to all the parties, to prove their respective averments, by leading evidence in support of the same.

7. In support of his case, the petitioner got himself examined as PW1, by way of evidence affidavit Ex.PW1/X, wherein he deposed that he is a practicing advocate,
and reiterated the contents of the FIR/DAR, regarding the manner of accident and injuries sustained by him in the case accident.
He further deposed that due to said impact, there was a total loss of his car, which was for a sum of Rs. 10,00,000/-.
PW1 further deposed that the offending vehicle belongs to Forensic Investigation Unit.
PW1 further deposed that due to the accident, he has sustained injuries on his hand and was not able to right properly, for about a month.

In his evidence, PW1 has placed reliance upon his ID card, as issued by Delhi High Court Bar Association as Ex. PW1/A, Copy of DAR as Ex. PW1/B (Colly.), Copy of MLC as Ex. PW1/C (OSR), Copy of his Aadhar Card as Ex. PW1/D (OSR), copy of his claim petition as Ex. PW1/1 and his income tax return for the assessment year 2019-20, along with computation sheet as Ex. PW1/E (four sheets).
8. PW1 was not been cross examined by the respondents, so as to elicit any admission from the testimony of PW1, in order to deny any rashness or negligence on the part of R1, resulting in the case accident.
9.
Final arguments were thereafter addressed by the petitioner.
No one has appeared on behalf of R1 and R2, for addressing arguments.
The issue-wise findings of this Tribunal based on appreciation of the evidence, are reproduced herein below.

Whether on 21.03.2019 at about 9:30 pm, at Maduban Chowk, Delhi, one Scorpio Car bearing registration No. DL-8CAT-5595, which was being driven rashly and negligently by R1/Ishwar Singh,
had hit the car bearing registration no. DL-8CNA-4905 and caused the injuries to Nawal Singh?
OPP 10.
The onus of proving this issue on preponderance of probabilities was upon the petitioner/claimant.
To prove the aspect of rashness and negligence of R1, in driving the offending vehicle, the petitioner got himself examined as PW1.
As per chargesheet, PW1 was himself the injured/eye witness of the case accident.

PW1 has led his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/X,
wherein he deposed that the accident has taken place, due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.

Further, perusal of the chargesheet reveals that the injured has made a Navwal Singh vs Ishwar on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189250524/
5 complaint dated 21.03.2019, to SHO PS Rani Bagh, wherein, he stated that the accident had taken place, due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, by R1.

11. R1 and R2 failed to contest the present DAR/claim petition, by filing any written statement, in their defence, consequently they both deemed to have admitted the entire contents of the DAR/
claim petition.

Further, they both failed to cross examine PW1, in order to highlight the weaknesses or to bring out any falsity, from the deposition of PW1, so as to negate the factum of accident, due to rashness or negligence, on the part of R1, in driving the offending vehicle.

12. The MLC of the injured, as annexed with the DAR, shows that after the accident, the victim was shifted to Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, on the same day, in emergency and at the relevant time, it was mentioned that the patient was victim of road traffic accident.
Further, as per MLC, the petitioner has sustained simple injuries in the case accident.

13. Thus, in view of the above said discussion, it can be safely concluded that the petitioner has been able to prove on preponderance of probabilities, that the case accident has been caused by R1, who was driving the offending vehicle, in a rash and negligent manner, at the above said date, time and place and had hit the petitioner, thereby causing simple injuries to him.
Issue no.1 is accordingly decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
Whether petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
OPP 14.

In view of the findings of this Tribunal, qua issue no. 1, regarding negligence of R1, resulting in the occurrence of the case accident, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the petitioner is entitled for compensation, in respect of medical expenses incurred by him, as well as pain and suffering endured by him, on account of injuries sustained in the case accident.

This Tribunal shall now examine the entire evidence led by the parties, including the documents of the petitioner, for the purpose of arriving at a finding about the quantum of compensation, to which the petitioner is entitled.
MEDICAL EXPENSES.

15. To prove the amount incurred by the petitioner, on his treatment, the petitioner got himself examined as PW1, by way of evidence affidavit Ex.PW1/X, wherein he deposed that after the accident, he received treatment from Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, vide MLC No. 782/19, dated 21.03.2019 but, he has not placed on record any medical treatment record/bills, so as to prove that he has incurred any expenditure, on his treatment, after the accident.

Since, PW1 has failed to place and prove on record, any medical bills or consultation fee/receipt, to prove payment of any amount to any doctor therefore, in the absence of any original receipt or medical bills of treatment, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled for compensation towards medical expenses.

Thus, this Tribunal deems it appropriate to award Nil compensation to the petitioner,
under this head of medical expenses.

sentences.text: To prove the amount incurred by the petitioner, on special diet and conveyance, the petitioner got himself examined as PW1, by way of evidence affidavit Ex.PW1/X, wherein he failed to quantify the amount, incurred by him on special diet and conveyance.

The petitioner has further failed to place on record, prescription of any doctor or medical practitioner or dietitian, containing details of special diet, such as, nutritional supplements, prescribed to him, for speedy recovery of the injuries,
sustained in the case accident.
He has also failed to place on record any transport bills, in respect of expenditure incurred by him, on his travel to hospital, from his residence and vice-versa.

Further,
the petitioner has also not examined any witness, to prove his expenditure on special diet and conveyance.

Accordingly, the entitlement of the petitioner, to compensation if any, towards special diet and conveyance charges, has to be determined, in accordance with the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner/victim in the case accident.

17. In this context, a perusal of MLC No. 782/19, dated 21.03.2019, of the petitioner Nawal Singh,
reveals that after examination of the petitioner, the doctor has given the observation, that there was swelling on his right forearm and tenderness over base of his right thumb and he was discharged from the said hospital on the same day.

Therefore, keeping in view the simple nature of injuries, as sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner must have incurred expenses on special diet, required for his speedy recovery, as well as on travel to clinics/hospitals from his residence and vice versa.
Accordingly, a lump sum amount of Rs. 10,000/- is granted to the petitioner, as compensation under this head, including Rs.5,000/- each, towards special diet and conveyance respectively.
ATTENDANT CHARGES 18.
It was argued by the petitioner that he has incurred expenditure on attendant charges.

However,
perusal of the record reveals that he has not disclosed the expenditure incurred by him, on availing services of a medical attendant, during his treatment period.

19. Further, perusal of the court record reveals that the petitioner has neither placed on record any bill, raised by any agency, from which, he had hired a medical attendant nor examined the concerned attendant, hired by him or any employee of the agency, through which, he had hired the said attendant.

However, as discussed above, regarding the medical condition of the petitioner, as per which, the petitioner has sustained simple injuries in the case accident therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that due to the injuries sustained by him, in the case accident, he must have availed services of at-least his family member, as an attendant for his self-care activities.
Thus, this Tribunal deems it appropriate to award a lump sum amount of Rs. 5,000/-, as compensation to the petitioner, under this head towards attendant charges.
PAIN AND SUFFERING 20.

In the present case, as per MLC No. 782/19 dated 21.03.2019, of the petitioner Nawal Singh, he had suffered simple injuries, in the case accident therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Navwal Singh vs Ishwar on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189250524/
7 petitioner must have suffered physical pain and mental agony, due to the injuries, sustained by him in the case accident.

LOSS OF INCOME

21.Petitioner Nawal Singh in his evidence has deposed that he is a practicing advocate and doing practice in Delhi High Court and District court since the year 1990 and due to the injuries sustained by him, in the case accident, he was not able to write properly for about a month.

In his evidence, he has placed on record, his ITR along with its computation, for assessment year 2019-20, as per which, at the time of accident, his net income, after deduction of tax was Rs. 5,41,757 - 35,424/-.
However, there has been no evidence led by the petitioner, to prove that there was any loss of income, sustained by him, due to the accident in question.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded to the petitioner, under this head.

22.Accordingly, the over all compensation, which is to be awarded to the petitioner comes to Rs.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
11. R1 and R2 failed to contest the present DAR/claim petition, by filing any written statement, in their defence, consequently they both deemed to have admitted the entire contents of the DAR/
claim petition.
Further, they both failed to cross examine PW1, in order to highlight the weaknesses or to bring out any falsity, from the deposition of PW1, so as to negate the factum of accident, due to rashness or negligence, on the part of R1, in driving the offending vehicle.
12. The MLC of the injured, as annexed with the DAR, shows that after the accident, the victim was shifted to Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, on the same day, in emergency and at the relevant time, it was mentioned that the patient was victim of road traffic accident.
Further, as per MLC, the petitioner has sustained simple injuries in the case accident.
In view of the findings of this Tribunal, qua issue no. 1, regarding negligence of R1, resulting in the occurrence of the case accident, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the petitioner is entitled for compensation, in respect of medical expenses incurred by him, as well as pain and suffering endured by him, on account of injuries sustained in the case accident.
Since, PW1 has failed to place and prove on record, any medical bills or consultation fee/receipt, to prove payment of any amount to any doctor therefore, in the absence of any original receipt or medical bills of treatment, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled for compensation towards medical expenses.
Accordingly, the entitlement of the petitioner, to compensation if any, towards special diet and conveyance charges, has to be determined, in accordance with the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner/victim in the case accident.
Therefore, keeping in view the simple nature of injuries, as sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner must have incurred expenses on special diet, required for his speedy recovery, as well as on travel to clinics/hospitals from his residence and vice versa.
, it is noteworthy that the Hon'ble Apex Court had in the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi vs. Association of Victims of Uphaar Tragedy, 2012 ACJ 48 (SC) had observed that the victims of Uphaar Tragedy be awarded compensation with interest @ 9% per annum.
Therefore, in the interest of justice, in the present case, this court is of the opinion that the claimant/petitioner is entitled to interest at the prevailing bank rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of DAR/petition, that is, with effect from 04.09.2019 till realization of the compensation amount.
In the case in hand, the offending vehicle is admittedly uninsured.
As per DAR, the offending was registered in the name of Director, FSL, Rohini, Delhi (hereinafter referred as R2) and Sh.
Prakash Chandra,
There has been no cross examination of the petitioner by R1 and R2, so as to dispute their liability.
Further, it has already came on record, that at the time of accident, R1 was driving the offending vehicle and the accident has been caused, due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.
Thus, both R1 and R2 are held jointly and severally liable, to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.
